  fills at full-stake loss; in each window the opposite quote did not fill or is unresolved.
  Packet numbers CONFIRMED, no discrepancies.
- DECISION 1 — the codex question (continue / alter / kill): CONTINUE, mechanically, to
  24 paper-quoted unique windows or 18:00Z per the 12:48 gate. Reasoning made explicit so it
  is not re-litigated at the next negative heartbeat: (a) 3 resolved fills is statistically
  nothing — even at fair 50% odds, 0-for-3 happens 12.5% of the time; (b) paper costs zero
  dollars, so the only thing early termination saves is wall-clock, and at the observed
  cadence (~5 windows / 27 min) the packet completes ~15:30-16:00Z, comfortably inside the
  gate; (c) a negative paper packet is a SUCCESSFUL measurement — it prevents a losing live
  lane; that is the packet doing its job, not the packet failing.
- DECISION 2 — do not touch the running measurement; augment the packet derivation only. At
  packet time, derive per-window fill topology from the existing orders list (no new
  instrumentation): both-sides-filled / one-sided-filled / none-filled counts, and PnL split
  by topology. The three losses above are all one-sided — classic maker adverse selection
  (the market fills you on the side it is moving against). Whether E7 has any edge is exactly
  the both-fill rate vs one-sided loss rate, and the data already sits in
  resolution_scoring.scored_orders + paper_quote_events. Zero code on the hot path.
- DECISION 3 — structural defect (found in this audit, pre-answering the likely packet
  failure): E7 sizes at fixed order_usd=8.0 PER SIDE. With equal DOLLARS, a both-sides-fill
  window costs $16 and pays 8/p_winner — profitable only when the underdog wins. The hedge
  property everyone assumes from quoting both sides at combined <1.00 (observed combined
  quotes: 0.99, 0.98, 0.99, 0.99, 0.99) only holds with equal SHARES: S shares per side costs
  S*(p_up+p_down) < S payout, guaranteed. So even a 100% both-fill E7 as parameterized is
  roughly coin-flip. Fix: implement `--paper-size-mode equal_shares` in the E7 runner and
  launch it as a PARALLEL paper variant E7.1 writing to e7_1_spot_open_paper_lane_* state
  files, same 30s offset, same zero-live guard. Start it as soon as implemented — it runs
  while the E7.0 packet finishes, so if E7.0 rules negative, E7.1's clock is already running
  instead of costing another day. Do NOT modify the running E7.0 lane or its files.

  E7.0 goes LIVE only if the packet shows resolved_paper_pnl_usd > 0 AND >= 12 resolved paper
  fills AND zero_live PASS AND CopyIntent parity intact; live start, if earned, is order_usd

  negative packets across E7 variants -> park E7 per the E6 precedent and log it.

- audit: with a wide hypothesis portfolio the dominant risk flips from
  slowness to FALSE EDGES (multiple-testing: enough hypotheses, noise
  looks like gold). Protocol ordered before results start arriving:
  1. ONE HARNESS: every study runs through a single standardized
     backtest harness — identical fill model, slippage, fees(=0),
     min-order floors, timestamp discipline. EV tables become directly
     comparable; no per-study methodology drift.
  2. LOCKED HOLDOUT: designated corpus periods (most recent 2 weeks +
     random weeks) are SEALED — no study touches them during search.
     A candidate only graduates by passing the sealed holdout ONCE,
     final-exam style. Peeking = the study is void.
  3. MULTIPLE-TESTING BAR: the out-of-sample significance threshold
     scales with the number of hypotheses tried (registered in a
     hypothesis ledger — every variant counts). Weak positives that
     would pass alone die when the family-wide bar applies. This is
     what separates us from every overfit retail bot.
  4. EVOI QUEUE: studies are prioritized by expected-value-of-
     information (potential edge x prior probability x cheapness), not
     FIFO — research compute allocated like capital, by Fable.
  5. ONE LEADERBOARD: all results land in a single standardized table
     (EV/trade, sample, t-stat, capacity estimate, holdout status) —
     the digest carries the top of it daily.
  6. TOP-K LIVE-PAPER: the best 5 candidates run permanently in paper
     against the LIVE feed regardless of corpus scores — regime-change
     insurance; corpus qualifies, live paper confirms, gates fund.

  right shape for the actual defect (kill the 9x redundancy), not merely a
  narrower first step. A read-only memoized cache was considered and
  rejected: with new events arriving every cycle, per-wallet writes would
  invalidate it repeatedly and leave the multi-write cost in place.
  Binding constraints:
  (1) Shape: load+parse the history state ONCE per guard cycle; parse the
      RTDS tail once and group matching rows by active wallet; run each
      wallet's dedupe/watermark/offset logic against the shared in-memory
      structure; sort/rebuild only if any wallet contributed new events
      (no-new-events fast path = skip dedupe/sort/serialize entirely);
      write the history state AT MOST ONCE per cycle, at end of premerge.
  (2) Ordering invariant: per-wallet RTDS offsets and observation
      watermarks may only advance after the history write (or the
      no-write fast path) succeeds — never persist an advanced offset for
      events that failed to reach the history state. This must be at least
      as safe as today's per-wallet ordering.
  (3) Parity: per-wallet summary fields (status, new_matching_events,
      retained_matching_rows, latest_event_ts/observed_ts, ingest_mode,
      offset evidence) must be preserved. Required test: a multi-wallet

      with new events, some without).

      residual needs a name before we decide whether a follow-up (e.g.
      compact serialization or splitting events from copy_intents/
      wallet_results in the 188MB file) is warranted.
  (5) Fold the recorded NITs: prune the duplicated per-wallet profile
      embedding (rows[] vs premerge_substage_profiles[]); bytes_requested==
      bytes_read stays informational.

     NOT "changes" — they act immediately as designed. Bug fixes
     restoring documented behavior may ship directly with the diff
     cited; anything that alters behavior goes through 1-4.

  dry-run lanes stay full-speed (they ARE the side branch). It slows
  exactly one thing: the last step onto the producing live path,

## 2026-07-10T19:07Z fable DIRECTION [SELF-DEV/LEARN] — BIZTOS-CHECK CAUGHT 2 METHODOLOGY HOLES IN THE VARIATION ENGINE. AMENDED BEFORE BUILD.
- HOLE 1 (moving-target parent): the live parent config CHANGES
  (rotations, denylist updates, sizing) while siblings run — naive
  sibling-vs-parent comparison would measure against a chimera of
  configs. AMENDMENT: comparisons are segmented by PARENT-CONFIG
  EPOCH (the change-journal/golden-snapshot id defines epoch
  boundaries); a sibling beats the parent only if it wins within
  epochs, never across a boundary.
- HOLE 2 (paper-fill flattery — the wallet-price illusion returning
  through the back door): siblings fill in the PAPER model while the
  parent fills LIVE; paper fills are systematically kinder, so a
  "winning" sibling might only be winning the fill-model. AMENDMENT:
  the parent gets a PAPER TWIN — an exact replica of the live config
  running in the same paper fill model as the siblings. The
  promotion bar becomes difference-in-differences: sibling must beat
  the PAPER TWIN by a margin (>=1pp ROI on n>=50), so the fill-model
  bias cancels out. The twin also doubles as a standing live-vs-paper
  calibration gauge (its gap to the live parent = the fill model's
  measured optimism, published on the scorecard).
- konzisztens: igen — both amendments implement the existing
  repricing doctrine (2026-07-07) inside the new engine; cost is one
  extra paper lane (the twin), budget declared at registration.

  the update when stale — no waiting for the operator.
- PROTOCOL (codex wires; composes with the version-smoke-test order):

     codex CLI's installed vs latest version; the codex heartbeat
     checks the claude CLI's (and grok's). Findings logged to
     cli_versions_state.json with a STALE flag.
  2. UPDATE EXECUTION RULES (the safety rails):
     a. ONE BRAIN AT A TIME — never update both CLIs in the same
        window: while one updates, the other stands as the healthy
        brain (the chain's redundancy is preserved through the
        update itself).
     b. QUIET-MOMENT ONLY: no update while any incident is open, a
        gate is within 30 min, or a canary is mid-flight.
     c. SMOKE TEST AFTER (already ordered): first post-update
        invocation verified rc+sanity; FAIL -> reinstall previous
        version (version pin recorded pre-update) + HANDOFF note.
     d. The trading layer needs no pause at any point (AI-free).
  3. SCOPE: brain CLIs first; critical runtime deps (py-clob-client
     etc.) monthly with the same rails + full test suite gate —
     dep updates are riskier than CLI updates and go through the
     PRODUCING discipline if they touch the hot path.

  redundancy-preserving sequencing is the new invariant; hot-path
  dep updates correctly routed through existing gates.

  the issubset test at :2075 and publishes LIVE_GUARD_BLOCKED/
  live_execution_arm_failed. Blast radius audited: in every
  affected cycle there were ZERO intents by definition of the
  trigger, so no order that should have been submitted was
  blocked; the guard self-recovered by 07:25Z without restart,
  liveness accepted_order 07:20:42Z, day green +10.158838. The
  defect corrupts a status signal, not order flow.

  patch and do NOT restart guard pid 9465 before R7 12:14Z.
  Reasoning, so it survives me: the fix is a one-line set
  addition but its deployment requires restarting the single
  live submitter. A restart carries nonzero re-arm risk and buys
  nothing before 12:14Z — recurrence costs a self-healing
  cosmetic blip we now fully understand, while a failed re-arm
  costs real order flow on a green day. The 06:48Z
  no-guard-changes-mid-clock order stands precisely for this
  trade: never spend live-path risk to fix a reporting-grade
  defect while the clock is running.

  during heartbeats before R7, if deadman/status shows

  filtered_candidate_copy_intents} (alone or with other benign
  keys) AND proof/operator/token blocker lists are empty, grade

  restart, do not notify, do not count it toward any drought or

  artifact): src/trade_executor.py `_market_buy_amount_with_valid_
  share_precision` searches downward for a cent amount whose
  implied shares fit CLOB 4-decimal precision; when no valid amount
  >= the $1.00 CLOB min exists at or below the requested size, it
  searches UPWARD (bounded by max_overshoot_usd=0.50). The
  wallet-copy policy cap on these drip orders is $1.00 — equal to
  the CLOB min — so at any price where $1.00 itself is not
  precision-valid, the only submittable amounts (e.g. $1.05, $1.29
  in live records) exceed the cap and the guard rejects locally
  with market_buy_precision_cap_exceeded. Deterministic dead zone:
  the frozen $1 drip size is UNDELIVERABLE at those prices. Live
  execution state shows 184 all-time occurrences; 44 today alone.
- RULING 23a (the fix — AUTHORIZED, defect class not sizing
  loosening): in the cap check (trade_executor.py ~line 934-939),
  when the ORIGINAL requested size_usd is within the policy cap and
  the excess comes solely from the precision/min-order adjustment,
  allow submission up to cap + max_overshoot_usd (0.50). Rationale:
  RULING 22a froze sizing INTENT; the $1 drip intent stands — this
  makes it executable at all prices instead of silently converting
  ~44 orders/day into guaranteed rejects. Worst-case extra exposure
  is $0.50 per order, bounded by the existing overshoot constant.
  Constraints: no other threshold/cap/eligibility change rides
  along; CopyIntent parity and single-submitter invariants
  untouched (change is inside the guard's executor); keep emitting
  market_order_amount_adjustment_usd; focused tests must cover the
  $1.00-cap-at-invalid-price case (reject before, submit after) and
  the still-rejected case (amount > cap + overshoot); full verifier
  before deploy. Report converted-reject count and their fill/PnL
  outcomes in the next STATUS. Expected effect: up to +44
  submittable orders/day against the 144/288 filled-window gap,
  with per-fill economics matching the existing fill population.

  governs DEPLOYMENT of already-tested-better solutions. It does NOT

  non-executable under the frozen $1 max_order + $1 CLOB min.

  precision-safe sizing — there is no size to adjust to: the
  executable band is [$1.00, $1.10] and for cent-prices whose
  numerator has a prime factor outside {2,5} with quantum > $0.10
  (0.43, 0.46, 0.47, 0.49, 0.41, 0.37, ...) that band contains no
  valid amount. Rounding down lands below CLOB min; widening the
  +$0.10 overshoot to admit $1.15-$1.41 is a 15-41% relaxation of
  the $1 cap by another name — DENIED. Maker fallback is also

- PRINCIPLE — COMPLEMENTARITY, NOT DUPLICATION: seats are added for
  COVERAGE UNION, selected by time-band complementarity (the temporal
  registry already classifies: 21 CONTINUOUS, 43 WEEKDAY-ONLY, 7
  WEEKEND-ONLY, 23 BAND-SPECIALIST). The roster is assembled like a
  24h mosaic: each new seat must add windows the current seats do NOT
  cover; hour_coverage union toward 288 is the selection metric,
  alongside its own positive copy-evidence.
- THE STEPWISE PATH (each step gated):
  S1 (at Phase 2 PASS): readiness packet = per-seat attribution,
  per-seat loss ladders (evidence-proportional per OP-ROSTER),
  allocator fair-floor math re-verified for N>1 — mostly existing
  machinery (eval-all flag, portfolio allocator, routing shadow).
  S2: max_live_seats 1->2 — the second seat is the highest-acceptance
  COMPLEMENTARY producer (disjoint active bands vs seat 1).
  S3: 2->4->8, each step gated on: aggregate PnL positive, clean
  per-seat attribution, and NO cross-seat interference — build the
  WINDOW COORDINATOR: one window, one seat (best signal wins the
  window; no two seats trade the same window against each other);
  the single guard remains the sole submitter, seats are internal.
  S4: DEAD-BAND COVERAGE to push toward 288: bands where NO copyable
  source is active get (a) mined band-specialists (the mine's
  temporal classes are the inventory) and (b) the STRUCTURAL engine
  (scalp does not need a source wallet — it fills windows copy
  cannot). Full 288 is a mosaic of copy-seats + structural windows.
- EDGE GAIN FROM MULTIPLICITY (why more seats = better edge, not
  just more volume): variance drops by diversification (LLN),
  per-window BEST-signal selection replaces one-wallet-everything,
  and the consensus lane (multiple sources agreeing) upgrades
  win-rate — all three already registered mechanisms.
- ORDER: this spec IS the multi-seat readiness packet's design
  input; codex builds the readiness packet against it at Phase 2
  PASS per the standing OP-SCALE-AXES-PRIORITY.

## 2026-07-21T19:20Z operator ORDER (Béla: "hogyan kényszerítsük ki még jobban a célt") + fable DIRECTION — THE THREE PRESSURE LEVERS: COMPETITION, PACE, DARWINIAN COMPUTE
- P-LEVER 1, INTERNAL COMPETITION FOR PRIMACY (binding): the copy
  lane holds primacy ONLY by outperforming. The structural engine
  (scalp) and every future engine are COMPETITORS, not backups: at
  each weekly verdict, measured $/day and $/heartbeat decide which
  lane is PRIMARY (gets first claim on seats/compute) for the next
  week. A lane that cannot win a week loses its crown by number, not
  by ruling. Succession is the sharpest known forcing function.
- P-LEVER 2, INTRADAY PACE-TO-BAR (binding, codex builds into the
  heartbeat): every heartbeat reports pace digits — day PnL and
  windows vs the TIME-PROPORTIONAL bar (e.g. at 12:00Z the pro-rata
  bar is ~$50 / ~72 windows). Falling below pace is not red by
  itself, but two consecutive pace-miss heartbeats REQUIRE a named
  same-day corrective (seat/band/amplification) — the day is
  corrected DURING the day, never only diagnosed at midnight.
- P-LEVER 3, DARWINIAN COMPUTE (binding, simple form): heartbeat
  and lane capacity allocation follows measured contribution —
  producing lanes get slots first; lanes with zero gated yield over
  their timebox surrender slots automatically. Compute is fed to
  what feeds the ledger.
- P-LEVER 4 (operator-side, recorded as intent): after today, rule
  restraint — the constitution is dense enough; the machine must own
  the goal under EXISTING law, and the operator's strongest
  remaining pressure is the weekly verdict read plus NOTIFY
  responses. Over-steering from here would compete with trading for
  the system's attention.
- konzisztens: igen — P1 is OP-ANYMETHOD's profit-loyalty made
  weekly-mechanical; P2 refines the daily bar to intraday
  granularity without new thresholds; P3 formalizes the existing
  utilization duty; P4 binds the humans, not the machine. Tonight's
  audit codifies these with the rest.

  split-inode race (holder flocked on the old inode, next writer creates
  and flocks a new file, both proceed -> two concurrent committers). The
  15:46Z boot audit's "stale_locks" finding is a classifier
  false-positive, not a remnant problem.
